about.title: Hanford Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a collision on Hanford roads changes everything, often overnight. Local corridors like N 11th Avenue, 12th Avenue, N 10th Avenue and 11th Avenue see a steady flow of traffic, and while Kings County's most recent count shows no traffic deaths alongside 80 injury collisions, any fatal outcome from a crash can open the door to a wrongful death claim. California law limits who may bring this type of civil action, generally starting with a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children, and extending to certain other dependents or heirs when no closer family exists. LawProactive doesn't handle these cases directly; instead, we connect grieving families in Hanford with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the circumstances, explain your options, and help you understand the deadlines that apply. There's no fee unless the attorney recovers something on your behalf. Reaching out costs nothing and starts the process of getting real answers during an incredibly difficult time.

whyChoose.title: Why Hanford Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California restricts standing in wrongful death cases to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible only when no closer family survives. An attorney can help clarify where your family fits before any claim moves forward.

items.title: Awareness of the Filing Deadline
items.desc: Wrongful death claims in California generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Missing this deadline can permanently close the door on a claim, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Clarity on What Losses Can Be Recovered
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of love, companionship and guidance. An independent attorney can walk through how these categories might apply to your family's specific loss.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none of those relatives exist, other dependents or heirs may be permitted to bring the claim instead. An attorney can review your family situation to confirm where you stand.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing someone in a Hanford crash?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims involving a government entity, such as a city road issue, often require action much sooner. Given how quickly these deadlines can arrive, it helps to get guidance early rather than waiting.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to any criminal charges from the crash?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, independent of any criminal case that may or may not be filed against the at-fault driver. Even if criminal charges are never brought, your family can still pursue a civil claim. An attorney can explain how the two processes typically unfold on separate tracks.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to help my family?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney; we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in the network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover something for your family.
